what: TransUnion is one of the three big credit bureaus. It holds credit files on hundreds of millions of people and sells reports and scores to lenders, and increasingly sells fraud-prevention and marketing data as well.
customers: Banks, card issuers, insurers, landlords, employers and telecom operators checking who they are dealing with.
money: credit reports, fraud tools and marketing data
bureaus in India, Africa, Latin America and the United Kingdom
credit monitoring sold directly to individuals
moat: A credit file assembled from decades of lender reporting that no newcomer can assemble, protected further by the regulation that governs who may hold it.
risks: Lending volumes drive report pulls, and mortgage lending is still weak
A data breach at a credit bureau is an existential event, as Equifax showed in 2017
opportunities: 18 times earnings with $910M of free cash flow, and analysts see about 22% upside
Revenue grew from $3.0B to $4.6B in four years, with India and Africa growing faster than the United States
Fraud prevention and identity verification grow with online commerce regardless of the lending cycle
watch: Mortgage inquiry volumes and growth in the non-lending data businesses.
